Why Async Python Matters

Asynchronous programming in Python has moved from a niche curiosity to a first-class part of the language. With asyncio baked into the standard library and frameworks like FastAPI embracing it, teams now reach for async def in ordinary backend code.

When async actually helps

The single most important rule: async only buys you concurrency for I/O-bound work. A web request that spends most of its time waiting on a database query or an HTTP call to another service is a great candidate. A CPU-bound loop that crunches numbers is not - the GIL still applies and you would do better with multiprocessing.

Common pitfalls

Forgetting to await a coroutine creates a silently-leaked task. Mixing blocking calls (think requests.get) inside an otherwise-async handler can stall the entire event loop. Tooling like anyio and the built-in asyncio.timeout() help, but discipline matters more than tools.
